current_example.problem: Carl walks $450$ meters in $5$ minutes. If he walks at a constant pace, at what rate does he walk?
current_example.worked_solution:
The ratio of meters to minutes that Carl walks is ${\color{blue}450}:{\color{red}5}.$ So we start with the ratio $450:5$ and write it as a fraction:

$$
\dfrac{{\color{blue}450}}{{\color{red}5}}
$$

We can make a denominator of $1$ by dividing the numerator and denominator by $5\mathbin{:}$

$$
\dfrac{{\color{blue}450}\div 5}{{\color{red}5}\div 5} = \dfrac{{\color{blue}90}}{{\color{red}1}}
$$

Therefore, Carl walks at a rate of $90$ meters per minute.
